evals.name: sec-template-core-anchor
evals.prompt: Run rust auditor on the vulnerable programs in {TARGET_PROJECT_PATH} (Ubuntu-Technologies/solana-security-template @cb48608, comments stripped per evals/benchmarks.md section 0): signer-authorization, owner-check, account-type-mismatch, insecure-init, duplicate-accounts, pda-security, account-close, arithmetic-overflow.
evals.expected_output: High findings matching the documented class per module: missing signer (B1), missing owner (B2), type cosplay (B3), re-init (B4), duplicate mutable accounts (B6), non-canonical/predictable PDA (B7). account-close has NO revival bug (Anchor 0.32.1 `close = owner` zeroes and reassigns) - a B8 finding there is a false positive. arithmetic-overflow: unchecked arithmetic PANICS (root overflow-checks = true), so at most a Low DoS, not a wrapping High; the ignored `_min_out` (B16) is the real bug. Found-by-skill (re-confirmed in code): duplicate-accounts authority never bound to from_account.owner; owner-check read_config compares the caller key with no is_signer; account-type-mismatch process_action reads the key at data[1..33] against a repr(C) layout with the key at 16..48, so it always fails (correctness, Low). No finding of a module's documented bug on its paired secure.rs. Under judging.md Gate 1 the module's missing is_signer check may also appear as its own finding masked by the T7 offset; that expectation has not been re-scored.
assertions: [source] B1 missing-signer on signer-authorization
[source] B2 missing-owner on owner-check
[source] B3 type-cosplay on account-type-mismatch
[source] B4 reinit on insecure-init
[source] B6 duplicate-mutable on duplicate-accounts
[source] B7 pda on pda-security
[not-present] no B8 revival finding on account-close (close = owner, anchor 0.32.1)
[source, reclassified] arithmetic-overflow overflow scored as panic / DoS (overflow-checks = true), not as a wrapping value bug
[source] B16 ignored _min_out on arithmetic-overflow swap_x_for_y
[found-by-skill] T3 authority not bound to from_account.owner on duplicate-accounts
[found-by-skill] T5 no is_signer on caller in owner-check process_read_config
[found-by-skill] T7 correctness: process_action offsets misread the User layout (always fails) on account-type-mismatch
no finding of the module's documented bug on its paired secure.rs

evals.name: sec-template-new-classes
evals.prompt: Run rust auditor on the account-griefing, authority-transfer, account-reloading, remaining-accounts and amm/buggy-amm programs in {TARGET_PROJECT_PATH} (solana-security-template @cb48608, comments stripped per evals/benchmarks.md section 0).
evals.expected_output: Leads/findings for: account-creation DoS via predictable init PDA (B13); single-step authority transfer (B14); unvalidated remaining_accounts (B5-adjacent); and in buggy-amm weak PDA seeds (B7) + unchecked overflow that WRAPS (the programs/amm workspace has no overflow-checks) (B10) + missing slippage / ignored min_out (B16). account-reloading has NO stale-after-CPI bug (vulnerable.rs makes no CPI) - a B11 finding there is a false positive. Found-by-skill (re-confirmed in code): buggy-amm deposit mints the caller's `amount` of LP regardless of the x/y paid (free LP with max_x = max_y = 0).
assertions: [source] B13 init-DoS on account-griefing
[source] B14 single-step-authority on authority-transfer
[not-present] no B11 stale-after-cpi finding on account-reloading (no CPI in vulnerable.rs)
[source] B5 unvalidated remaining_accounts on remaining-accounts
[source] B16 missing-slippage on buggy-amm swap
[source] B10 overflow on buggy-amm scored as wrapping (amm workspace has no overflow-checks)
[found-by-skill] T1 deposit mints amount LP independent of x/y paid on buggy-amm

evals.name: escrow-pinocchio-destination-validation
evals.prompt: Run rust auditor on the p-escrow Pinocchio program in {TARGET_PROJECT_PATH} (solana-security-template @cb48608, comments stripped per evals/benchmarks.md section 0).
evals.expected_output: A High finding that the refund destination is not validated against the stored maker, letting a refund be redirected to an attacker (destination/recipient validation, B15/L2) - a native/Pinocchio manual-validation miss. Found-by-skill (re-confirmed in code): process_secure_refund requires destination == caller (the maker's wallet) and token-transfers to it, so the secure refund fails for every caller and escrowed tokens cannot be refunded.
assertions: [source] refund destination not checked against escrow.maker
[found-by-skill] T9 process_secure_refund always fails (destination must equal the caller wallet)
